hints.title: ASCII Difference Between Upper and Lower Case
hints.text: In standard encoding, every uppercase letter differs from its lowercase counterpart by exactly bit 5, representing integer value 32.

hints.title: Setting Bit 5 with Bitwise OR
hints.text: Applying a bitwise OR with 32 turns uppercase characters into lowercase while leaving lowercase letters and non-alphabet characters unaffected.

hints.title: Iterating Characters and Translating Range
hints.text: For each character in s, check if its code point lies between capital A and capital Z. If so, apply bitwise OR with 32 to lowercase it; else keep unchanged.

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving linear O(N) time and linear O(N) output space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Built-in methods hide lower-level encoding rules that interviewers frequently query.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Translating characters directly via bit manipulation avoids allocating conversion lookup tables.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should understand character encoding values and the binary relationship between case representations.
